script.base: Low-event outdoor game: market has Minnesota -3.5 with implied totals MIN 19.5 and CLE 16.0, so a modest Minnesota lead and a late run lean, not a shootout. J.J. McCarthy is out and the offensive line is missing Brian O'Neill, Ryan Kelly, Donovan Jackson and Michael Jurgens, so the pass game should be short and checkdown-heavy behind Jordan Mason (41 carries, 203 yards in weeks 2-4) rather than a Jefferson shot day. Cleveland, a 3.5 dog with Joe Flacco, leans on Quinshon Judkins (49/237) early and throws more only if it trails.
script.flip1: Cleveland leads early. Minnesota abandons the run, Mason's carry script dies, and the unnamed backup quarterback is stuck in obvious passing behind a shorthanded line — Hockenson checkdowns become the offense and deep air-yard players (Jefferson 283 air, Nailor 167 air) are the ones at risk.
script.flip2: Minnesota is up two scores and clocks it. Mason's carry count spikes and a rush under dies even at a low yards per carry; Hockenson and Jefferson targets stall after halftime. An unsaved wind or rain downgrade would push this further into a slog.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost. Hockenson lost because the unnamed backup forced Jefferson (who had 24 targets and 282 yards in the prior three games) and Minnesota's 19.5 implied total showed up as a run-out win, leaving the tight end on 12-15 yards again. Mason lost because a modest lead became a clock-kill, he got 20 carries, and one of the few 10-plus runs Cleveland does allow turned 55 expected yards into 70-plus, the same shape as his 68 and 116 games. The counter-case is strongest on Mason, which is why that lean is efficiency-tagged and not strong. Inactives and weather were not in the pack; a late Jones promotion or a Newsome scratch would have been the checkpoint that rewrites this.
slip_story: One low-total slog story, not a shootout stack: Minnesota's shorthanded line produces short throws (Hockenson over 27.5) and an inefficient Mason rush (under 62.5) against a 2.94 YPC front. Do not add Jefferson, Nailor or Jeudy overs — those need the deep game this script kills. Do not add a game over. Judkins over would need the opposite run-defense story and stays off the slip. No bet placed.
